newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-HENMAN COMES FROM BEHIND TO BEAT SIEMERINK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN COMES FROM BEHIND TO BEAT SIEMERINK.

text.p: Briton Tom Henman came from behind to win a tight and tense two and a half hour battle with Dutchman Jan Siemerink and reach the quarter-finals of the Lyon Grand Prix on Thursday.
The Wimbledon quarter-finalist won the second round match 6-7 7-6 7-6 after being a set and 4-1 down, then said he had taken better advantage of the few really decisive points.

"When you're both serving well, the match turns on a few points that you must take advantage of and I took better advantage tonight," said Henman, world number 32 and ranked eight places above Siemerink.
"At the start of the third set, I was very disappointed to get broken when I had come back to one set all.
"Things were going badly and I told myself I had to win my service and I would then have opportunities on his. And when I went 3-2 up I made four good shots and felt things were going better."
The crucial point in the last tiebreak came when Siemerink netted an easy volley with Henman at his mercy and, instead of going to 5-5, gave the Briton two match points.
The Dutchman saved the first on his service but then Henman made no mistake when he sent down another booming first serve which Siemerink returned wide to give him the match.

Earlier, French Davis Cup player Arnaud Boetsch went through when Russian Andrei Chesnokov retired with a pulled thigh muscle as the Fenchman was poised to serve for the second set after losing the first in a tiebreak.
